findings.title: The 5s timeout covers only the run-scope close, not the rest of stop()
findings.body:
`instance.stop({ timeout })` passes the timeout only to `closeRun` (apps/desktop/src/backend/DesktopBackendManager.ts:1087, 366-369). Earlier steps in `stop` have no bound:
- `mutex.withPermits(1)` at line 1051.
- `spec.onShutdown` at line 1077.
- `Fiber.interrupt(restartFiber)` at line 1081.

`start` holds the same mutex across `spec.configResolve`, `fileSystem.exists`, and `spec.onPreflightFailed` (lines 691-800). If one of those hangs, for example a WSL config resolve while the VM boots, the quit finalizer waits on the mutex with no limit. `markComplete` never runs and quit hangs, which is the symptom this PR is meant to remove. The new test only hangs the process-scope finalizer, so it does not cover this. If you want the "guarantee the quit path makes progress" claim in the comment at line 148 to hold, wrap each `instance.stop(...)` in `Effect.timeoutOption(...)`. Alternatively, say in that comment that only the process teardown is bounded.

After the timeout, each instance's own layer finalizer (`Effect.addFinalizer(() => stop())` at DesktopBackendManager.ts:1157) calls `stop()` again with no timeout. That does not hold up quit, because `markComplete` has already fired, but the second teardown is unbounded.

findings.title: A new quit-path test lives in the backend manager test file and imports DesktopApp
findings.body: The test exercises `DesktopApp.stopAllPoolInstances`, but it sits in `DesktopBackendManager.test.ts` and pulls `../app/DesktopApp.ts` into the backend test module. That is the wrong direction for the dependency. A test next to `DesktopApp` (for example `app/DesktopAppErrors.test.ts` or a new `DesktopApp.test.ts`) would be a better home. This is not a defect: `DesktopAppErrors.test.ts` already imports `DesktopApp.ts` without mocking electron, so the import is safe.

contracts.action: Quit finalizer now stops every pool instance with a 5s timeout through the new `stopAllPoolInstances`, followed by `markComplete`
contracts.equivalent_path: The pre-quit-and-install path in DesktopUpdates already calls `instance.stop({ timeout: Duration.seconds(5) })` on every pool instance concurrently, so this change copies it.
contracts.before_after: Before, the finalizer called `instance.stop()` with no timeout, so a hung backend teardown blocked `markComplete`, and `awaitComplete` in DesktopLifecycle blocked quit. Now `closeRun` forks the scope close into the parent scope and waits at most 5s (DesktopBackendManager.ts:366-369). The finalizer returns, `Effect.ensuring(markComplete)` fires, and quit proceeds. The forked close keeps running in the background.
contracts.visible_effect: The app quits within about 5s plus the unbounded pre-close steps, even when a backend process teardown hangs.
contracts.failure_mode: If the timeout elapses, `closeRun` returns false. `stop` then skips state cleanup (removeControlSource, discardSession) at lines 1088-1090, which is fine at quit. Steps before the timeout (mutex acquisition, onShutdown, restart-fiber interrupt) remain unbounded. See the finding at line 154.

contracts.action: What bounds the whole quit wait
contracts.before_after: `Effect.forEach` runs the stops concurrently with a 5s timeout per instance, so the wall-clock bound for the run-scope close is 5s total, not 5s per instance. The mutex acquisition, `onShutdown`, and `Fiber.interrupt(restartFiber)` come before the timeout and have no bound of their own. The mutex is held by `start` during config resolve, an fs exists check, and `onPreflightFailed`.
contracts.visible_effect: In the worst case, a hang in one of those pre-close steps still blocks quit, with no timeout.
contracts.failure_mode: Quit hangs because `markComplete` is never reached.
contracts.open_question: Can `spec.configResolve`, `fileSystem.exists` or `onPreflightFailed` hang long enough in practice (WSL cold start) to hold the mutex during quit?

summary: The change is small and correct for what it targets. `stopAllPoolInstances` passes a 5s timeout to every pool instance's `stop`, runs them concurrently, and `markComplete` still fires through `Effect.ensuring`. This matches the existing pre-quit-and-install code in DesktopUpdates. The new test is deterministic: it uses queues and `TestClock`, and it runs the helper as a scope finalizer, as the quit path does. I have one consider-level finding: the timeout bounds only the run-scope close inside `stop()`, so a hang while acquiring the mutex or in `onShutdown` would still block quit. The test also sits in the backend manager file while testing a DesktopApp function. I have no risk facts or judgement calls to report.
